title: Document evidence and exact answer
goal: Locate the requested document evidence and faithfully transcribe the requested answer
guidance:
Use the original image as evidence. Resolve three things together: what entity or relation the question targets, where the corresponding evidence is, and which part of that evidence constitutes the requested answer. Determine the requested scope first, then transcribe that selection faithfully. A concise answer excludes unrequested context; it does not delete characters within the selected text. Follow the applicable steps below internally; output only the answer.

1. Select the source by the question's relation. On a form, match the printed field label and follow its box, line or keyed block to the value. Distinguish sender from recipient, home from office, claimed from paid, current from previous, and person from employer. A field can contain several roles: identify them separately and return only the role asked for. A document's publisher or letterhead is not automatically the company named in a person's company field. On a page with several headings, distinguish publication/series name, document title, section heading and item title. Match the requested level instead of selecting the largest text. For document-type questions, use explicit type words and the document's structure; letterhead alone does not make a document a letter. Spatial qualifiers such as top, bottom or beside select the evidence region.

2. Read the selected relation completely. For tables, fix the table, row and column, including subheaders, time period and population, before reading the cell. A question can be a table lookup even without the word table. For comparisons, first restrict to the requested group, then compare the requested measure across all eligible entries; distinguish an absolute value, difference and proportion. Return the winning entity if the question asks which entity, and the value if it asks how much. Copy an explicitly printed total when it is the requested value; compute only when a derived result is actually requested. For lists and contents, anchor to the named section, count the requested ordinal in its order and keep the entry separate from its marker and associated page. For multi-part questions, include each requested item, without adjacent unrelated fields.

3. Set the answer boundary by its type. A person's title is the title, not an adjacent employer or address. A company name keeps the words belonging to that name. A type, category or product variant is its complete distinguishing phrase, not just its first modifier. Keep name components that distinguish one product line or variant from another. A report title is its printed title, not an explanatory synonym in parentheses. For a date component such as year, return that component; for a date, preserve the document's date notation. For a count or revision number, return the requested value without its introducing label (including No. or #). For a printed compound page locator containing both current page and total pages, preserve that whole locator unless the question explicitly requests just one component. For a lone page numeral, decorative framing is not part of the number. For a structured identifier or telephone number, preserve the actual digits, leading zeros and internal punctuation. Do not expand abbreviations or replace source spelling with a familiar name.

4. Keep value notation distinct from context. Preserve the decimal precision, signs and separators of the selected value. Keep a currency symbol or unit that is printed as part of that value or its dedicated value field. Do not import a symbol from another row, a shared column header or general knowledge. A bare numeric table cell remains bare when its unit is only in the heading; use that heading to identify the correct column, not to append words to the answer. An explicit request for a numeric component or particular representation controls the output. Read written-out amounts in their printed form. Separate filled amount components from unused template text: a blank denomination is not an additional amount, while a question specifically asking about an empty/none field may require its visible zero/none marker.

5. Resolve actual visual ambiguity without inventing certainty. First confirm the selected field or table position, then inspect the ambiguous letters or digits in that same region. Nearby fields are context, not replacements for its value. Distinguish visually similar characters from their strokes; do not correct a name or identifier to the most familiar spelling. Preserve handwritten notation instead of inserting standard punctuation. On forms, separate handwritten strokes from printed rules, dotted leaders, boxes and scan noise. Compare a disputed mark with the surrounding template; preserve genuine punctuation, and inspect the selected region when this distinction is visually unresolved. When the target is clearly legible and uniquely matched, proceed directly; do not reopen an established reading merely to generate alternatives.

6. Submit the complete requested selection faithfully. For printed quotations, slogans and titles, preserve punctuation attached to the selected phrase, including enclosing quotation marks when they are present in the image. Do not add quotation marks merely because the answer is text. Do not add the supporting sentence, field label, explanation, inferred synonym or an unrequested neighboring value. A sentence introducing a study or item can begin with an article that is not part of its name; retain articles that actually belong to a proper name or title. Do not shorten a complete name or category by deleting an identifying word. Keep all requested members of a list. Do not change the selected entity or answer type during final wording. Return only the answer text.
